cards.name: Verdure 1
cards.summary: Vector pattern-fill style from the Vonster set: baroque acanthus-leaf scrolls and curling flourishes in golden yellow over a red ground with faint darker-red tonal swirls; no visible outline or effect. The pattern tiles at a fixed size, so the star shows one leaf spray and the letters only fragments of scrolls. (Thumbnail: the style applied by script with applyTo to a 5-point star and to 'PGD' type converted to outlines, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: ornate festive or holiday greeting graphics
vintage label, packaging or folk-art accents
decorative fill for big display letters, badges or crests
avoid: small text or thin shapes: the motif is large, so letters show only fragments of it; use on big shapes or heavy display type
expecting the pattern to scale with the object: pattern fills keep their tile size unless Transform Patterns is on (Scale dialog or Preferences > General)
cards.applies_to: closed paths, compound paths, groups, live or outlined type with a fill area; open paths and hairlines show almost nothing. Graphic style of 3 fills and 1 stroke, no live effects or brushes: layered pattern-swatch fills that replace the object's appearance (no outline shows in the thumbnail); the style must exist in the target document.
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: Window > Graphic Style Libraries > Vonster Pattern Styles, select an object, click 'Verdure 1' (Alt-click adds it to the current appearance instead of replacing it). Script: app.open("C:/Program Files/Adobe/Adobe Illustrator 2026/Presets/en_US/Graphic Styles/Vonster Pattern Styles.ai"), doc.graphicStyles.getByName("Verdure 1").applyTo(pageItem) on an item in that document, item.duplicate(target.layers[0], ElementPlacement.PLACEATEND) (the style arrives in the target document), then close the library with SaveOptions.DONOTSAVECHANGES.

verified.note: Golden-yellow acanthus scrolls over red with faint darker-red swirls fill the star and the PGD letters, no outline.

review.changes: none

cards.name: 16 Colors
cards.summary: Image Trace preset: colour trace limited to 16 colours (read back: colour mode, 16 colours, abutting fills, noise 15). On the test photo it gives a posterised, flat-shape picture: beige-tan wall, dark brown-charcoal shadows, red stripes, maroon panels with cream tops; mid-tone detail simplifies into blotchy flat patches (still readable) and fine detail drops out. Identical to [Low Color] on the test photo apart from a handful of pixels (same settings). (Thumbnail: the photographic test plate, placed, traced and the preset loaded by script with loadFromPreset, not a shipped preview.)
use_for: flat-colour illustration from a photo
limited-colour poster or screen-print art
clip art or flat graphics to clean vector
avoid: portraits where faces matter: skin breaks into blotchy flat patches; use [High Color] or [Auto-Color]
large or high-resolution photos: tracing is slow and makes thousands of paths; downsample the image first
cards.applies_to: placed (linked or embedded) raster images: PlacedItem or RasterItem. The trace becomes a live tracing object whose result is vector paths; expand it to get editable paths. Does nothing on vector art.
cards.how_to_apply: Panel: select the image, Window > Image Trace, choose '16 Colors' from Preset (or the Image Trace preset menu in the Control / Properties bar), then Object > Image Trace > Expand for editable paths. Script: var t = placedItem.trace(); t.tracing.tracingOptions.loadFromPreset("16 Colors"); then t.tracing.expandTracing() to convert to paths.

verified.note: Posterised flat-colour trace: tan wall, red stripes, maroon panels, but the dark areas are dark brown-charcoal (no navy anywhere) and the mid-tone detail stays readable as blotchy patches.

review.changes: summary: 'navy' -> 'dark brown-charcoal' for the darkest areas, mid-tone detail 'mottled brown blobs' -> 'blotchy flat patches (still readable)', 'pixel-identical to [Low Color]' -> 'identical apart from a handful of pixels'; avoid: no longer points to High Fidelity Photo (its frame is untraced)
